{"problem": {"theorem": "Let \( N \) be a positive integer. Two persons play the following game. The first player writes a list of positive integers not greater than \( 25 \), not necessarily different, such that their sum is at least \( 200 \). The second player wins if he can select some of these numbers so that their sum \( S \) satisfies the condition \( 200-N \leq S \leq 200+N \). What is the smallest value of \( N \) for which the second player has a winning strategy?", "assumptions": [], "domain": "baltic_mo", "explicit_subgoals": []}, "candidate_text": "The smallest value is \(\boxed{11}\).

To prove necessity, let the first player write five copies of \(23\) and four copies of \(24\). Their total is
\[
5\cdot23+4\cdot24=211.
\]
Every proper sublist has sum at most \(211-23=188\), while the whole list has sum \(211\). Hence no selectable sum lies in \([190,210]\), so \(N=10\) does not suffice. Consequently no smaller \(N\) suffices either.

For sufficiency, consider any list of positive integers at most \(25\) whose total is at least \(200\). Add its entries in any order until the partial sum first reaches or exceeds \(189\). If the resulting sum is \(s\), then the preceding partial sum is at most \(188\), so
\[
189\le s\le188+25=213.
\]
If \(s\le211\), the selected entries already have sum in \([189,211]\).

It remains to treat \(s=212\) or \(s=213\). If \(s=212\), some selected entry is at most \(23\): otherwise all selected entries would lie in \(\{24,25\}\), but at most eight such entries sum to at most \(200\), while at least nine sum to at least \(216\), so their sum cannot be \(212\). Removing an entry at most \(23\) leaves a sum between \(189\) and \(211\).

If \(s=213\), some selected entry is at most \(24\), since a sum of copies of \(25\) cannot equal \(213\). Removing that entry leaves a sum between \(189\) and \(211\).

Thus every permitted list has a subset whose sum satisfies
\[
200-11=189\le S\le211=200+11.
\]
Therefore \(N=11\) is sufficient and, by the construction above, minimal."}
